primary_claim: Scaling the activation-steering coefficient K per-layer proportionally to that layer's mean residual-stream L2 norm (K_l = mean_norm_l / sqrt(d)) keeps relative injection strength constant across layers and models, and this norm-calibrated K improves safety-steering scores across four instruction-tuned model families, with all models collapsing at the same relative K-multiple (x3) regardless of architecture.

effect.metric: safety score (%) under positive norm-calibrated steering at K x1, vs unsteered baseline
effect.value: Qwen and Gemma peak at 97.3% and 100% respectively at K x1 (vs unsteered baselines of 89.6% and 98.9%); all models collapse at K x3

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies prior activation-steering practice of using a flat K value across all layers or a single high-K layer, which the author says yielded gibberish output or failed steering because relative injection strength rho_l = K/||h_l|| decays with depth as residual norm grows
stated_future_work: investigate how models recover from very high steering magnitudes and produce coherent output when they have enough remaining layers to reconstruct the response
publish a blog post and code linking HuggingFace to demo the 'baked-in' model with the steering direction written into the MLP down_proj bias
quote: all models improve under positive steering (qwen and gemini peaks at 97.3%, 100% with $K$ x 1), and degrade under negative, Every model collapses at $K$ x 3
